answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with staked vouching: every new identity locks a bond and earns vouches from trusted agents, each vouch counting for less as it ripples outward. A forger may mint a whole spiral of fake names, but cannot vouch for itself, so each leaf needs a fresh bond while its trust shrinks. Catch one duplicate and the bond is slashed - a loss as sharp as crystal - which compounds across the cluster. Like yarrow knitting loose soil, these cross-links tie identity to real history, so each extra name costs more than the influence it buys.
